instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

typeRaw.description: Forge-reported account type, retained verbatim for callers that classify further.

isBotHint.description: Hint derived from forge metadata that the actor is automation. Callers own the classification policy.

app.description: The app behind a bot account, where the forge ties one to it (GitHub Apps' `slug[bot]` users).

Actor.description: An account: a user, an organisation or a bot.

AuthKind.description: The credential types that a provider can accept.

sha.description: The commit that the branch points at.

previousPath.description: Path before a rename or copy.

patch.description: Unified diff for the file, where the forge returns one inline.

isBinary.description: The file is binary, so it has no patch.

ChangedFile.description: A file that a commit or pull request changed.

conclusionRaw.description: Forge-native conclusion, where the forge reports one apart from the status.

Check.description: One check on a commit: a check run, a commit status, a job or a policy evaluation.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

type.description: What the id addresses: a check run, a commit status, a CI job, or a branch policy evaluation.

CheckRef.description: One check run, commit status or CI job.

CheckState.description: `neutral` covers skipped and informational results, which neither pass nor fail.

total.description: Absent when the forge reports only a combined state.

ChecksSummary.description: Combined state of the checks on a pull request's head commit. `failure` when any check failed, else `pending` while any runs, else `success`.

stage.description: Stage or group the job belongs to, where the forge has one.

CiJob.description: One job of a CI run.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

CiJobRef.description: One job inside a run. `run` is absent when the job was addressed on its own.

number.description: Per-repo run number, where the forge has one.

eventRaw.description: What triggered the run, as the forge names it.

sha.description: The commit that the run ran on.

CiRun.description: A CI run, such as a workflow run or a pipeline.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

CiRunRef.description: A CI run: a workflow run, a pipeline, or a build.

roleRaw.description: Forge-native role name, for example `maintainer` or `reporter`.

Collaborator.description: An account with a role on a repository.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

id.description: Forge-native comment id; an AT-URI on Tangled.

CommentRef.description: Reference to a comment on a thread.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

sha.description: The full sha of the commit.

CommitRef.description: A commit addressed by its full sha.

actor.description: The account, where the forge can match it.

date.description: When the commit was authored or committed.

CommitSignature.description: Git authorship, with the forge account behind it where the forge matched one.

base.description: The revision that the comparison starts from.

head.description: The revision that the comparison ends at.

aheadBy.description: The number of commits that `head` has and `base` lacks.

behindBy.description: The number of commits that `base` has and `head` lacks.

commits.description: The commits between the two revisions.

mergeBaseSha.description: The merge base, where the forge reports it.

nextUrl.description: Absolute URL of the next page, from a `Link` header or the body, on the requested origin.

etag.description: A validator for a conditional request.

token.description: Opaque forge-native cursor, for example a GraphQL `endCursor`.

Cursor.description: Opaque-ish resumption token. Fields are optional because forges differ in what they support; callers should persist the whole object and hand it back.

EventAction.description: What happened, independent of `kind`, so "anything that closed" is `action === 'closed'` whatever the subject.

EventDetail.description: Typed detail for an event. Discriminated by `type`.

path.description: The path from the repository root.

sha.description: Blob sha, where the forge reports one.

url.description: Web page for the file at this ref, where the forge has one.

content.description: Bytes, as a `Uint8Array`. JSON cannot carry them.

path.description: The path from the repository root.

sha.description: Blob sha, where the forge reports one.

url.description: Web page for the file at this ref, where the forge has one.

FileContent.description: A file's contents. Narrow on `encoding` to get text or bytes.

FileStatus.description: How a commit or pull request changed a file.

version.description: Instance version the capabilities were computed for, when known.

experimental.description: The provider as a whole has not reached parity: hand-authored fixtures only, or an unstable upstream.

sources.description: `subscribe` is a long-lived push stream; see {@link SourcesApi}.

list.description: Support for `threads.list()` and `threads.listPage()`, per thread kind.
Support for `threads.comments()` and `threads.commentsPage()`, per thread kind.
Support for `threads.reactions()` and `threads.reactionsPage()`, per thread kind.

reactions.description: Listing the reactions on a thread or one of its comments, per thread kind.

upsertComment.description: Composed from `comment`, `comments.list` and `comments.edit`, so always `'emulated'` where it works at all.

react.description: Support for `threads.react()` and `threads.unreact()`, per thread kind.

writes.description: Write verbs, per thread kind except `merge`, `approveAndMerge`, `transfer` and `markDuplicate`.

set.description: Support for `threads.subscribe()` and `threads.unsubscribe()`, per thread kind.

subscriptions.description: Reading a thread subscription (`get`) and changing it (`set`), per kind. Distinct from notification unsubscribe.

checks.description: `thread` covers `Thread.checks` and `threads.checks()` (pull requests only); the rest are the commit-level surface. `report` is a commit status unless the credential can write check runs.

ci.description: Read-only CI surface. `log` is `false` where job logs are not reachable over the API.

reviews.description: Reviews on a pull request. `list` is `'emulated'` where reviews are synthesised from approvals or votes; `create` then covers only the events the forge's approval endpoint can express.

contents.description: Repository contents. `tree` is `'emulated'` where recursion is walked level by level rather than by the forge.

webhooks.description: Managing registered webhooks, beside receiving deliveries.

search.description: Cross-repository search of issues and pull requests, repositories and commits. No code search.

securityAlerts.description: Per alert kind, since each needs its own token scope on GitHub.

installations.description: Enumerating app installations and deriving one provider per installation.

eventKinds.description: `'heuristic'` when event kinds are inferred from free text (GitLab system notes) rather than reported by the forge, so `kind` may be `'other'` or wrong for unrecognised wording; `kindRaw` and `payload` stay exact.

authKinds.description: Auth types the provider accepts. The type this provider was created with is `ForgeProvider.authKind`.

limits.description: Maximum text lengths the forge accepts.

ForgeCapabilities.description: What a provider supports, operation by operation. It is computed without a request, and `refreshCapabilities()` refines it with the instance version. Each group holds one entry per capability, and the [capability matrix](/reference/capability-matrix) lists them for every forge.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

kindRaw.description: Forge-native event name the normalised `kind` was derived from.

action.description: Normalised verb; `other` when the forge's wording has no equivalent.

summary.description: Single line describing the event, suitable for a list row.

detail.description: The details that belong to the kind of event.

installationId.description: App installation the delivery belongs to, for app webhooks.

source.description: Delivery mechanism the event arrived through.

payload.description: Unnormalised forge payload, retained for fidelity.

ForgeEvent.description: An event on a forge, such as a comment, a state change or a push.

ForgeInstance.description: Host of a single forge deployment, for example `github.com` or `codeberg.org`.

ForgeKind.description: Identifier of a forge implementation. Unknown forges are permitted so that third-party providers can be registered without a core release.

message.description: A description of the problem, for a person.

subject.description: Key or URI of the item the warning concerns, when it concerns one.

ForgeWarning.description: A non-fatal problem encountered while producing a result.

ForgeWarningCode.description: The warning codes providers emit; providers may add codes in a minor release.

GetManyResult.description: One `threads.getMany()` entry, in input order; narrow on `ok`.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

targetTypeRaw.description: Forge-native target type, for example `Organization` or `User`.

repositorySelectionRaw.description: Forge-native repository selection, for example `all` or `selected`.

Installation.description: An app installation on an account, with its own credential scope.

repositorySelection.description: Whether the token reaches all repositories or only selected ones.

InstallationToken.description: A short-lived token that acts as one app installation.

KnownForgeKind.description: The forges this package ships providers for.

colour.description: The colour as hex digits, without a leading `#`.

Label.description: A label that a repository defines.

MergeMethod.description: How a pull request is merged.

id.description: Forge-native milestone id, as `threads.setMilestone` takes it.

reason.description: Why the account got the notification.

reasonRaw.description: Forge-native reason string. Absent when the forge reports no reason at all.

subjectTypeRaw.description: Forge-native subject type, for example `PullRequest`, `Release` or `followed`.

subjectState.description: State of a thread subject as reported by the notification payload.

raw.description: Unnormalised forge payload, retained for fidelity.

Notification.description: A notification of the authenticated account.

NotificationReason.description: Why a notification was delivered. `'unknown'` covers forges that report no reason and native reasons with no normalised equivalent; `reasonRaw` keeps the original.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

id.description: Forge-native notification identifier, used for read/done/unsubscribe writes.

NotificationRef.description: Reference to a notification. Distinct from {@link ThreadRef}: a notification is a per-user delivery record whose lifetime and identity are independent of the thread it points at.

NotificationSubject.description: What a notification is about. Not every notification concerns a thread.

PerKind.description: Per-thread-kind support. `'other'` subjects have no verbs, so they have no entry.

repo.description: The repository that holds the head branch, which differs for a fork.

head.description: `sha` is absent on forges where a pull is a patch rather than a branch (Tangled).

mergeCommitSha.description: The merge commit, once the pull request is merged.

PullBranches.description: The branches of a pull request.

PushCommit.description: A commit as a push delivery reports it.

content.description: `'other'` where the forge's name has no entry in {@link ReactionContent}.

contentRaw.description: The forge's own name for the reaction, such as a GitLab award emoji or a Forgejo emoji.

Reaction.description: One reaction left on a thread or a comment, as `threads.reactions()` lists them.

ReactionContent.description: The reactions every forge with reactions has in common, named as GitHub names them. A forge-native name with no entry here is not reported.

total.description: The number of reactions of every kind.

counts.description: The number of reactions of each kind.

viewerReacted.description: Reactions the authenticated account has left. Absent when the forge does not report them.

ReactionSummary.description: The reactions on a thread or comment, counted.

ref.description: Absent where the forge publishes a download URL but nothing to address the asset by.

ReleaseAsset.description: A file attached to a release.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

id.description: Forge-native asset id; the asset name, or the link id, on forges that have no asset id.

ReleaseAssetRef.description: A release asset, addressable for download with `releases.downloadAsset`.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

id.description: Forge-native release id; the tag name on forges that key releases by tag.

ReleaseRef.description: A release, as a notification subject or event target.

displayName.description: The repository's name where `ref.name` is an identifier rather than the name (a Tangled record key).

isArchived.description: The repository is archived and read-only.

parent.description: The repository that this one was forked from.

topics.description: Topics, also called tags, that describe the repository.

cloneUrls.description: Git remotes. Tangled maps the hosting knot to its SSH host.

pushedAt.description: Last push, where the listing endpoint reports it.

openIssueCount.description: Open issues only, never combined with pull requests. Absent where the forge reports only the combined count (GitHub).

openPullCount.description: The number of open pull requests, where the forge reports it.

owner.description: The account or organisation that owns the repository, where the forge reports one.

language.description: Primary language, as the forge detects it.

homepage.description: Project website, apart from the repository's own `url`.

licence.description: SPDX identifier of the licence the forge detects, for example `MIT`.

watchers.description: Accounts watching the repository's activity, apart from stars.

permissions.description: What the authenticated account may do.

mergeMethods.description: Merge methods the repository allows, where the forge reports them. Empty means the forge reported none.

Repo.description: A repository as every forge reports it. Fields that not every forge has, such as `openPullCount`, are optional.

RepoFeatures.description: Which subjects a repository has switched on, where the forge makes them per repository.

maintain.description: Manage the repository without access to sensitive or destructive settings.

triage.description: Manage issues and pull requests without write access.

RepoPermissions.description: The authenticated account's access to a repository.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

owner.description: Full namespace path. On forges with nested groups (GitLab) this contains slashes, for example `acme/platform`; `name` never does.

name.description: Repository name. Empty for namespace-scoped refs.

kind.description: `'namespace'` for subjects that belong to a group rather than a repository (GitLab epics). Absent means a repository.

externalId.description: Stable forge-native identifier that survives renames and transfers: a GitHub, Forgejo or Gitea numeric id, a GitLab project or group id, a Bitbucket UUID or a Tangled repo DID. {@link repoKey} prefers it over `owner` and `name`.

RepoRef.description: Addresses a repository by its forge, instance, owner and name.

RepoRole.description: A collaborator's role, highest first. `'none'` is an explicit absence of access.

comments.description: Inline comments submitted with the review. `false` where the forge has approvals but no review objects to hang comments on.

Review.description: A review of a pull request.

line.description: Line in the file the comment is anchored to, in the side it is anchored to.

side.description: `'left'` is the base of the diff, `'right'` the head.

inReplyTo.description: Forge-native id of the comment this one replies to.

thread.description: The resolvable conversation the comment belongs to, where the forge has one.

ReviewComment.description: A comment left on a line of the diff as part of a review.

startLine.description: First line of a multi-line comment.

ReviewCommentInput.description: An inline comment to send with a review.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

id.description: Forge-native review id; a synthesised `approval:<login>` where the forge has approvals but no review objects.

ReviewRef.description: Reference to a review on a pull request.

ReviewState.description: What a review or a reviewer says about a pull request. `unknown` is a state that the model does not name.

isTeam.description: True when the reviewer is a team rather than an account.

Reviewer.description: A reviewer who was asked to review a pull request, and what they said.

title.description: A short description of the problem.

package.description: `ecosystem` is absent where the forge reports only the package name.

SecurityAlert.description: A security alert on a repository.

SecurityAlertKind.description: What an alert is about. `other` is a kind that the model does not name.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

id.description: Forge-native alert id. GitHub numbers each alert kind separately, so `kind` is needed to address one.

SecurityAlertRef.description: A security alert: a vulnerable dependency, a code scanning result, a leaked secret or an advisory.

SecuritySeverity.description: How severe an alert is. `unknown` is a level that the model does not name.

SourceKind.description: How an event reached the caller.

SubscriptionState.description: Whether the account gets notifications for a thread.

Support.description:
Capability flag. Every value other than `false` means the operation is available:

- `true`: native, and verified against a recording of the forge's responses.
- `'emulated'`: composed from other calls, so the result is approximate.
- `'experimental'`: native, but either unverified against the live forge or built on an API the forge marks unstable.

sha.description: Commit the tag points at, after dereferencing an annotated tag where the forge does so.

TextLimits.description: Maximum lengths the forge accepts, in characters.

stateRaw.description: Forge-native state string the normalised `state` was derived from.

stateReason.description: Forge-native state qualifier, for example `completed` or `not_planned`.

reviewers.description: Reviewers the thread read reports. Some forges report outstanding requests only, others each reviewer's verdict; `threads.reviews()` has every submitted review.

lastActivityAt.description: Latest activity the forge reports for the thread.

participants.description: Everyone who authored or commented on the thread, where the forge reports them.

readState.description: Whether the authenticated account has read the thread, where the forge tracks it per thread.

subscription.description: The authenticated account's subscription, where the thread read already carries it.

stack.description: Pull requests in a stack: a chain of dependent pull requests, each based on the one before.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems hit while reading the thread, for example an unreachable record.

raw.description: Unnormalised forge payload, retained for fidelity.

Thread.description: An issue, pull request, discussion or commit conversation.

ThreadKind.description: Kind of thread. `'other'` holds forge-specific subjects with no shared kind (check suites, epics); `typeRaw` names them.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

typeRaw.description: Forge-native subject type, for example `PullRequest` or `MergeRequest`.

number.description: Per-repo thread number, the commit sha for `kind: 'commit'`, or the forge-native id for `kind: 'other'`. Absent when the forge did not identify the thread; such a ref cannot be fetched or keyed until enriched.

displayNumber.description: Human-facing per-repo number, when it differs from `number`. Tangled identifies threads by AT-URI but shows numbers in its UI and webhooks.

externalId.description: Globally unique forge-native identifier, where one exists: a GitHub `node_id`, a GitLab global id, or an atproto record URI.

ThreadRef.description: Reference to a thread. A thread `number` is unique only within its repo, so the repo is always carried alongside it.

id.description: Forge-native stack id, where the forge names stacks.

parent.description: The pull request this one is stacked on. Absent for the root of the stack.

ThreadStack.description: Where a pull request sits in a stack of pull requests.

ThreadState.description: Thread state. `'unknown'` is distinct from any real state and signals that the value was not present in the payload, so the caller may enrich it with `threads.get()`. Draft status is orthogonal; see `Thread.isDraft`.

path.description: Path from the repository root, without a leading slash.

size.description: The size in bytes, for a file.

mode.description: POSIX mode as the forge reports it, for example `100644`.

TreeEntry.description: One entry of a repository tree.

comment.description: The comment that was created or edited.

created.description: `false` when an existing comment with the same key was edited.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

typeRaw.description: Forge-reported account type, retained verbatim for callers that classify further.

isBotHint.description: Hint derived from forge metadata that the actor is automation. Callers own the classification policy.

app.description: The app behind a bot account, where the forge ties one to it (GitHub Apps' `slug[bot]` users).

User.description: A user or organisation account, as `users.get()` reads it.

events.description: Normalised kinds the subscription covers, derived from `nativeEvents`.

nativeEvents.description: Forge-native event names exactly as the forge stores them.

contentType.description: `'json'` or `'form'` where the forge offers a choice.

secret.description: Never returned: no forge reads a webhook secret back.

Webhook.description: A registered webhook. The secret is never readable, so it is never returned.

event.description: Forge-native event name of the delivery.

status.description: The HTTP status that the receiver answered with.

ok.description: `true` when the forge considered the delivery successful.

duration.description: Round trip in milliseconds, where the forge reports it.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

guid.description: Delivery guid, where the forge needs it to redeliver.

WebhookDeliveryRef.description: Reference to one delivery of a webhook.

instance.description: The host of the instance, such as `github.com` or `git.example.com`.

target.description: The repository or namespace that the hook is registered on.

WebhookRef.description: Reference to a registered webhook. `target` is the repository, or a namespace ref (`kind: 'namespace'`, empty `name`) for an organisation or workspace hook.
